title: Memory Allocations, Leaks, and Bitmap Pressure Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies memory allocations, leaks, and bitmap pressure?
options: Find the ownership or allocation mechanism and prove bounded memory across repeated realistic lifecycles.
Judge leaks from one large object
questions.answer: Find the ownership or allocation mechanism and prove bounded memory across repeated realistic lifecycles.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A large object in a heap dump is necessarily a memory leak.
questions.explanation: Replacing a strong reference with WeakReference without fixing ownership hides the lifetime contract and can cause data to disappear unpredictably.

questions.answer: An object remains reachable through an unintended retaining path after its useful owner lifecycle has ended.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
